title: A picture inside a request is matched byte for byte, so an agent that shows the model a screenshot misses on the next run
foundBy: session agent replaying a multi-member campaign through cs-vcr, several replays at a time on one shared host
details:
**What happened.** An agent in a recorded campaign takes a screenshot of a web page and shows it to the model. The picture travels inside a request, as `messages[].content[].image_url.url` holding base64 data. On a busy host the second rendering differed by three bytes out of about fifteen thousand, and the replay missed at that step twice in a row. `cs-vcr calibrate` named the path from the real miss, and declaring it under `normalize.extend.volatile` cured it.

**Why it matters.** `cs-vcr` already matches loosely on what a tool printed, because that is an observation of the world and not a decision. A picture a tool took is the same kind of thing. It is only compared exactly because it sits in a field that the shipped rules do not know. Every agent with a browser or a vision tool will meet this, and each author will have to find it through a miss. A rule written for one path covers one path. A picture in a tool result, or in another provider's content block, would miss again.

**What is asked for.** Treat an inline image or other binary payload as a volatile observation in the rules `cs-vcr` ships, for each surface it knows. The OpenAI form is `image_url` with a `data:` address, and the Anthropic form is an `image` block with a base64 `source`. Say so in the manual beside the text on changed tool output.

**How to reproduce.** Record a session in which the agent sends a screenshot to the model. Replay it on a machine under other load, with `--dump-misses`, and run `cs-vcr calibrate` on the result.

notes.text: The rules are written and tested on the branch `image-volatile`, and the record stays open. CONTRIBUTING.md asks for a ruleset change to bump `normalize.version` and re-record every committed fixture in the same change. That recording needs three API keys and two subscription logins, and has not been run.

What the branch ships differs from the request in one way. The record asks for a `data:` address to be tolerated. A volatile rule is a path, and SPEC rule R11 forbids inferring volatility from a value. So the OpenAI paths `messages[].content[].image_url.url` and `input[].content[].image_url` also tolerate a changed remote address, and report it as drift. The Anthropic path is `messages[].content[].source.data`, which leaves a `url` source exact.

The branch covers more than pictures, as the record's words `other binary payload` allow. It names Anthropic `document` blocks, OpenAI chat `file` and `input_audio` parts, and OpenAI responses `input_file` parts. A picture inside a tool result needed nothing, because the shipped tool result paths already cover it. The text beside a picture stays exact, and a test holds that on all seven shapes.
